questions.stem:
Figure 1 shows a sketch of the curve with equation $y=x\ln x$, $x \geqslant 1$. The finite region $R$, shown shaded in Figure 1, is bounded by the curve, the $x$-axis and the line $x=4$.

The table shows corresponding values of $x$ and $y$ for $y=x\ln x$.

$\begin{array}{|c|c|c|c|c|c|c|c|}\hline x & 1 & 1.5 & 2 & 2.5 & 3 & 3.5 & 4\\ \hline y & 0 & 0.608 & & & 3.296 & 4.385 & 5.545\\ \hline\end{array}$

parts.label: a
parts.text:
(a) Complete the table with the values of $y$ corresponding to $x=2$ and $x=2.5$, giving your answers to 3 decimal places.
(2)

parts.label: b
parts.text:
(b) Use the trapezium rule, with all the values of $y$ in the completed table, to obtain an estimate for the area of $R$, giving your answer to 2 decimal places.
(4)

parts.label: c
parts.text:
(c) (i) Use integration by parts to find $\int x\ln x \, dx$.

(ii) Hence find the exact area of $R$, giving your answer in the form $\frac{1}{4}(a\ln 2+b)$, where $a$ and $b$ are integers.
(7)
parts.mark_scheme:
(c)(i) $\int x\ln x \, dx=\frac{x^2}{2}\ln x-\int \frac{x^2}{2}\times\frac{1}{x}\,dx$ M1 A1
$=\frac{x^2}{2}\ln x-\int \frac{x}{2}\,dx$
$=\frac{x^2}{2}\ln x-\frac{x^2}{4}(+C)$ M1 A1
(ii) $\left[\frac{x^2}{2}\ln x-\frac{x^2}{4}\right]_1^4=(8\ln4-4)-\left(-\frac{1}{4}\right)$ M1
$=8\ln4-\frac{15}{4}$
$=8(2\ln2)-\frac{15}{4}$ $\ln4=2\ln2$ seen or implied M1
$=\frac{1}{4}(64\ln2-15)$ $a=64,b=-15$ A1

questions.stem:
The curve $C$ has the equation
$\cos 2x+\cos 3y = 1$, $-\frac{\pi}{4} \leqslant x \leqslant \frac{\pi}{4}$, $0 \leqslant y \leqslant \frac{\pi}{6}$

parts.label: b
parts.text:
The point $P$ lies on $C$ where $x=\frac{\pi}{6}$.

(b) Find the value of $y$ at $P$.
(3)
parts.mark_scheme:
(b) At $x=\frac{\pi}{6}$, $\cos\left(\frac{2\pi}{6}\right)+\cos3y=1$ M1
$\cos3y=\frac{1}{2}$ A1
$3y=\frac{\pi}{3}\Rightarrow y=\frac{\pi}{9}$ awrt 0.349 A1

parts.label: c
parts.text:
(c) Find the equation of the tangent to $C$ at $P$, giving your answer in the form $ax + by + c\pi = 0$, where $a$, $b$ and $c$ are integers.
(3)
parts.mark_scheme:
(c) At $\left(\frac{\pi}{6},\frac{\pi}{9}\right)$, $\frac{dy}{dx}=-\frac{2\sin2\left(\frac{\pi}{6}\right)}{3\sin3\left(\frac{\pi}{9}\right)}=-\frac{2\sin\frac{\pi}{3}}{3\sin\frac{\pi}{3}}=-\frac{2}{3}$ M1
$y-\frac{\pi}{9}=-\frac{2}{3}\left(x-\frac{\pi}{6}\right)$ M1
Leading to $6x+9y-2\pi=0$ A1

questions.question_text:
The curve $C$ has the equation
$\cos 2x+\cos 3y = 1$, $-\frac{\pi}{4} \leqslant x \leqslant \frac{\pi}{4}$, $0 \leqslant y \leqslant \frac{\pi}{6}$
(a) Find $\frac{dy}{dx}$ in terms of $x$ and $y$.
(3)
The point $P$ lies on $C$ where $x=\frac{\pi}{6}$.

(b) Find the value of $y$ at $P$.
(3)
(c) Find the equation of the tangent to $C$ at $P$, giving your answer in the form $ax + by + c\pi = 0$, where $a$, $b$ and $c$ are integers.
(3)
questions.mark_scheme_text:
(a) $-2\sin2x-3\sin3y\frac{dy}{dx}=0$ M1 A1
$\frac{dy}{dx}=-\frac{2\sin2x}{3\sin3y}$ Accept $\frac{2\sin2x}{-3\sin3y}$, $\frac{-2\sin2x}{3\sin3y}$ A1
(b) At $x=\frac{\pi}{6}$, $\cos\left(\frac{2\pi}{6}\right)+\cos3y=1$ M1
$\cos3y=\frac{1}{2}$ A1
$3y=\frac{\pi}{3}\Rightarrow y=\frac{\pi}{9}$ awrt 0.349 A1
(c) At $\left(\frac{\pi}{6},\frac{\pi}{9}\right)$, $\frac{dy}{dx}=-\frac{2\sin2\left(\frac{\pi}{6}\right)}{3\sin3\left(\frac{\pi}{9}\right)}=-\frac{2\sin\frac{\pi}{3}}{3\sin\frac{\pi}{3}}=-\frac{2}{3}$ M1
$y-\frac{\pi}{9}=-\frac{2}{3}\left(x-\frac{\pi}{6}\right)$ M1
Leading to $6x+9y-2\pi=0$ A1

parts.label: b
parts.text:
(b) Given that $y=8$ at $x=1$, solve the differential equation
$\frac{dy}{dx} = \frac{(9x+6)y^{\frac{1}{3}}}{x}$
giving your answer in the form $y^2=\mathrm{g}(x)$.
(6)
parts.mark_scheme:
(b) $\int \frac{1}{y^{\frac{1}{3}}}\,dy=\int \frac{9x+6}{x}\,dx$ Integral signs not necessary B1
$\int y^{-\frac{1}{3}}\,dy=\int \frac{9x+6}{x}\,dx$
$\frac{y^{\frac{2}{3}}}{\frac{2}{3}}=9x+6\ln x (+C)$ $\pm ky^{\frac{2}{3}}=$ their (a) M1
$\frac{3}{2}y^{\frac{2}{3}}=9x+6\ln x (+C)$ ft their (a) A1ft
$y=8, x=1$
$\frac{3}{2}8^{\frac{2}{3}}=9+6\ln1+C$ M1
$C=-3$ A1
$y^{\frac{2}{3}}=\frac{2}{3}(9x+6\ln x-3)$
$y^2=(6x+4\ln x-2)^3$ $\left(=8(3x+2\ln x-1)^3\right)$ A1

questions.notes: [ms_verify] (b) '=\\int(9x+6)\\,dx$' -> '=\\int \\frac{9x+6}{x}\\,dx$' (MS p.7: Official page shows the integrand as (9x+6)/x, not 9x+6)
questions.question_text:
(a) Find $\int \frac{9x+6}{x} \, dx$, $x>0$.
(2)
(b) Given that $y=8$ at $x=1$, solve the differential equation
$\frac{dy}{dx} = \frac{(9x+6)y^{\frac{1}{3}}}{x}$
giving your answer in the form $y^2=\mathrm{g}(x)$.
(6)
questions.mark_scheme_text:
(a) $\int \frac{9x+6}{x}\,dx=\int\left(9+\frac{6}{x}\right)dx$ M1
$=9x+6\ln x (+C)$ A1
(b) $\int \frac{1}{y^{\frac{1}{3}}}\,dy=\int \frac{9x+6}{x}\,dx$ Integral signs not necessary B1
$\int y^{-\frac{1}{3}}\,dy=\int \frac{9x+6}{x}\,dx$
$\frac{y^{\frac{2}{3}}}{\frac{2}{3}}=9x+6\ln x (+C)$ $\pm ky^{\frac{2}{3}}=$ their (a) M1
$\frac{3}{2}y^{\frac{2}{3}}=9x+6\ln x (+C)$ ft their (a) A1ft
$y=8, x=1$
$\frac{3}{2}8^{\frac{2}{3}}=9+6\ln1+C$ M1
$C=-3$ A1
$y^{\frac{2}{3}}=\frac{2}{3}(9x+6\ln x-3)$
$y^2=(6x+4\ln x-2)^3$ $\left(=8(3x+2\ln x-1)^3\right)$ A1

parts.text:
The area $A$ of a circle is increasing at a constant rate of $1.5\,\mathrm{cm^2\,s^{-1}}$. Find, to 3 significant figures, the rate at which the radius $r$ of the circle is increasing when the area of the circle is $2\,\mathrm{cm^2}$.
(5)
parts.mark_scheme:
$\frac{dA}{dt}=1.5$ B1
$A=\pi r^2 \Rightarrow \frac{dA}{dr}=2\pi r$ B1
When $A=2$
$2=\pi r^2 \Rightarrow r=\sqrt{\frac{2}{\pi}} (=0.797884...)$ M1
$\frac{dA}{dt}=\frac{dA}{dr}\times\frac{dr}{dt}$
$1.5=2\pi r\frac{dr}{dt}$ M1
$\frac{dr}{dt}=\frac{1.5}{2\pi\sqrt{\frac{2}{\pi}}}\approx0.299$ awrt 0.299 A1

questions.stem:
Figure 2 shows a sketch of the curve $C$ with parametric equations
$x=5t^2-4$, $y=t(9-t^2)$
The curve $C$ cuts the $x$-axis at the points $A$ and $B$.

parts.label: a
parts.text:
(a) Find the $x$-coordinate at the point $A$ and the $x$-coordinate at the point $B$.
(3)
parts.mark_scheme:
(a) $y=0 \Rightarrow t(9-t^2)=t(3-t)(3+t)=0$
$t=0,3,-3$ Any one correct value B1
At $t=0$, $x=5(0)^2-4=-4$ Method for finding one value of $x$ M1
At $t=3$, $x=5(3)^2-4=41$
(At $t=-3$, $x=5(-3)^2-4=41$)
At $A$, $x=-4$; at $B$, $x=41$ Both A1

parts.label: b
parts.text:
The region $R$, as shown shaded in Figure 2, is enclosed by the loop of the curve.

(b) Use integration to find the area of $R$.
(6)
parts.mark_scheme:
(b) $\frac{dx}{dt}=10t$ Seen or implied B1
$\int y\,dx=\int y\frac{dx}{dt}\,dt=\int t(9-t^2)10t\,dt$ M1 A1
$=\int(90t^2-10t^4)\,dt$
$=\frac{90t^3}{3}-\frac{10t^5}{5}(+C)$ $\left(=30t^3-2t^5(+C)\right)$ A1
$\left[\frac{90t^3}{3}-\frac{10t^5}{5}\right]_0^3=30\times3^3-2\times3^5$ $(=324)$ M1
$A=2\int y\,dx=648$ $(\mathrm{units^2})$ A1
